/look_brief.audience: Brindle Markets' executive team (chief executive, finance, property, retail operations and commercial directors), who know their own store P&Ls and will test every figure against them before committing capital
/look_brief.occasion: a five-page section of a store format strategy pre-read, read on laptops and printed the evening before a steering committee, then talked through page by page at the table; it is not projected to a hall
/look_brief.subject_world: grocers run on the shelf-edge ticket (one bold price with its unit price in small type underneath), the planogram and the aisle number. The pages borrow the ticket's habit for the so-what column (a figure in bold with its unit line under it) and the aisle number as a two-digit section code in each kicker, which orders the five steps of the argument; they leave out produce greens, gingham, basket and fruit icons and receipt-style mono type, which would be costume with no job and read as a marketing deck to a board weighing closures
/look_brief.data_character: a store-level estate of 214 stores by four formats, with sales, invested capital, cash return and catchment growth per store; a regional market by five channels over three points in time; five customer segments by four measures; a three-year EBITDA bridge and a phased programme. Two exhibits per page, each pair a deliberate comparison (market against behaviour, P&L against return, segment value against Brindle's share, the estate against the actions), plus a so-what column or band

density.target: dense consulting: two exhibits and a so-what column per page, 180 to 260 words a page, a 214-point store scatter, tables of 5 to 11 rows at 8pt
density.why: a pre-read is read at the reader's own pace and checked line by line; an executive team deciding closures needs each claim and the evidence for it on one page, so splitting a claim from its proof onto another page would cost more than the density does

/look_brief.look: editorial consulting: white pages, Gelasio serif claim titles in near-black over Inter text, Brindle's own figures in deep navy, the market and unchanged stores in a cool grey-blue, one persimmon only where each claim lands, ruled tables with no fills, and a pale warm panel holding the so-what figures like shelf tickets

colour_meanings.color.accent1: Brindle's own figures and the latest period, and the page structure: kicker codes, figures in the so-what column
colour_meanings.color.accent3: context that recedes: the market, earlier periods, stores the plan leaves unchanged
colour_meanings.color.accent2: the place the claim lands on each exhibit: the series, bar, segment or stores the title names
colour_meanings.color.emphasis: the same persimmon as accent2, for a look-here outline or line that marks where the claim lands
colour_meanings.color.positive: a signed gain, only in the EBITDA bridge
colour_meanings.color.negative: a signed loss, only in the EBITDA bridge
colour_meanings.color.surface_alt: the so-what panel and a table's block heads, never data
colour_meanings.color.ink_muted: units lines, sources, axis labels: everything a reader consults and does not read first

/look_brief.type_ladder: built from the densest page, the network page: a 214-point scatter beside an 8-row action table of seven columns and a so-what column on a 13.33 in page; the table sets only at 8pt cells, so cells and headers are 8pt, axis and data labels 7.5pt, sources and footnotes at the 7pt floor (Inter has a large x-height, read at 7pt on screen); body 9pt for the so-what text, exhibit heads 10pt bold, a 20pt Gelasio claim title that holds a 15 to 22 word claim on two lines, and a 20pt Gelasio ticket figure in the so-what column

rejected.what: topic titles with the claim in a lead-in
rejected.why: the section argues for closures and capital; an executive reads the titles in sequence as the argument, which only claim titles carry

rejected.what: a navy title band across the top of every page
rejected.why: it is the loudest thing on the page and carries no data; a thin rule closes the title zone instead

rejected.what: one hue per store format across the deck
rejected.why: four format hues would give colour four meanings and spend the persimmon; formats are named in table rows and point labels

rejected.what: header fills and row banding on the tables
rejected.why: at 8pt on dense pages fills read as stripes and compete with the exhibits; a heavy rule under the header and hairlines do the separating
values are labelled on the marks, and the scatter's only lines that matter are the hurdle and the catchment threshold

rejected.what: big-number KPI tiles across the top
rejected.why: a figure alone loses its base; each so-what figure carries its unit line and the comparison under it

/description.summary: Editorial consulting: white pages, Gelasio claim titles over Inter, navy for Brindle, grey-blue for context, persimmon where the claim lands, a warm so-what panel.
/description.typography: Gelasio 20pt bold claim titles and ticket figures; Inter for everything else on a 10, 9, 8, 7.5, 7pt ladder.
/description.color: Navy leads, grey-blue recedes, persimmon marks the claim; green and red only for signed bridge steps.
/description.layout: 0.45 in margins, a kicker code and two-line claim title above a thin rule, two exhibits per page with a so-what column or band.
/description.tables: No fills; a heavy rule under the header and at the foot, hairlines between rows, block heads on the warm panel colour.
/description.motifs: the two-digit section code in the kicker and the shelf-ticket figure in the so-what panel

/continuation.why: a page that splits repeats its title with (continued) after it
